solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Engineer chap getting work

parts.note: a chap is a man
oeuvre is French for a work, used in English for an artist's output

explanation.surface: An engineer, a fellow, lands himself a job.
explanation.definitionFit: To engineer something is to contrive or steer it skilfully, which is what to manoeuvre means as a verb.

clue.text: One sculpting "Mother and Child"

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
a son is a child

explanation.surface: Someone at work carving a statue titled Mother and Child.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks suggest an artwork's title, but the two words are simply the two pieces, in order.
explanation.definitionFit: A mason dresses and carves stone, so the craftsman is literally one who sculpts.

clue.text: Arctic swimmer raced north with Prince Harry

indicators.note: in a down clue, going north means the word for raced is read upwards, back to front

parts.note: raced means ran
Hal is the nickname of Prince Harry, the future Henry V, in Shakespeare's history plays

explanation.surface: Some polar creature swam north alongside a royal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'north' is a reversal signal because this is a down entry: RAN read upwards gives NAR.
explanation.definitionFit: The narwhal is a tusked whale of Arctic waters, so it is a swimmer found there.

clue.text: Save Hebridean island lake that's remarkable

parts.note: save in the sense 'apart from' means except
Iona is an island in the Inner Hebrides off western Scotland
L is the abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: Rescue a striking loch on a Scottish island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Save' reads as a verb meaning rescue, but it is the preposition meaning except.
explanation.definitionFit: Something exceptional stands out from the ordinary, the same idea as being worthy of remark.

clue.text: 500 idle, maybe, for spell in Caribbean

parts.note: 500 is written as the digits 5, 0, 0; 5 is the Roman numeral V and each zero looks like the letter O
to be idle is to do nothing: DO followed by O for nothing

explanation.surface: Five hundred people loafing about while under a Caribbean spell.
explanation.walkthrough: 500 is read digit by digit, not as the Roman D, and idleness is 'do nothing', with O as nothing; the blogger called it outrageous but a write-in.
explanation.definitionFit: Voodoo is the folk religion of Haiti, known for its spells and charms, so a spell there can be called voodoo.

clue.text: Obscure English drunkard at Morecambe?

parts.note: a sot is a habitual drunkard
Eric Morecambe was half of the much-loved British comedy double act Morecambe and Wise; the question mark marks the hint by example

explanation.surface: An unknown English boozer turns up in the seaside town of Morecambe.
explanation.walkthrough: Morecambe looks like the Lancashire seaside town; it is the comedian's surname, so his first name is wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: Esoteric knowledge is understood only by a small circle, so it is hard to grasp, or obscure.

clue.text: Emperor's hearing complaint tavern ignored

indicators.note: ignored means the tavern word is left out of the complaint

parts.note: tinnitus is a ringing in the ears
an inn is a tavern

explanation.surface: A Roman ruler suffers ringing ears and gives the pub a miss.
explanation.definitionFit: Titus was a Roman emperor, son of Vespasian, who reigned briefly in the first century AD.

clue.text: Add up as well as down

definitions.text: Add up as well as down

parts.words: Add up as well as down
parts.note: a word meaning to total that reads the same upwards and downwards in the grid

explanation.surface: Total a column of figures going up and then going down.
explanation.walkthrough: To tot up is to add; the word is a palindrome, so it reads the same up or down the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: To tot up figures is to total them, a British informal verb for adding a list together.

clue.text: Capital consumption is breaking bailiff's heart

parts.note: consumption is an old name for tuberculosis, TB

indicators.note: breaking means the word is splits those central letters
heart of means the letters at the centre of the bailiff word are taken

explanation.surface: A disease is breaking a court officer's heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'consumption' is the old name for TB; 'heart' here takes three central letters, not one, and 'breaking' splits them.
explanation.definitionFit: Tbilisi is the capital city of Georgia in the Caucasus.

clue.text: Turn chopped fungi over for observer

indicators.note: over means the whole combination is read backwards
chopped means the word for turn loses its last letter

parts.note: to turn is to rotate
ceps are edible mushrooms, porcini

explanation.surface: Someone flips sliced mushrooms in the pan while another person watches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chopped' trims the last letter from the turn word, leaving ROTAT, and 'over' reverses everything, mushrooms included.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectator watches an event without taking part, the same as an observer.

clue.text: Hot wind from Morocco is back for the moment

indicators.note: for means one thing stands in place of another

parts.note: taken as written
MO is short for moment, as in 'half a mo'

indicators.note: back means the word is is read backwards

explanation.surface: A hot wind blowing out of North Africa returns briefly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is back' gives SI, which goes 'for' (in place of) MO, the moment, in MOROCCO.
explanation.definitionFit: The sirocco is a hot, dusty wind that blows from North Africa across the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Sketch feature of Rugby, swapping parts

indicators.note: swapping parts means the two halves of the rugby term change places

parts.note: a lineout is the rugby restart where players line up to contest a throw-in

explanation.surface: Draw a characteristic scene from Rugby School, rearranging bits of it.
explanation.walkthrough: Capital-R Rugby suggests the school or town; it is the game, where a lineout restarts play. LINE and OUT trade places.
explanation.definitionFit: An outline is a rough sketch or summary, giving the main shape without detail.

clue.text: Play character in first book, missing third

indicators.note: missing third means the third letter of that name is dropped

parts.note: Noah appears in Genesis, the first book of the Bible

explanation.surface: A dramatic role in an opening volume, with the third act absent.
explanation.definitionFit: Noh is a classical Japanese form of masked musical drama, so a type of play.

clue.text: Person regularly needing rope to control alien mob

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter of person is taken
a rope to control something goes round it, so the alien sits inside the rope word

parts.note: a lariat is a lasso, a rope
ET is the film alien

explanation.surface: Someone needs a rope to restrain an extraterrestrial crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: The proletariat is the working masses, and mob is a disparaging word for the common people.

clue.text: Number Ten has ruined European continent's housing

indicators.note: housing means the continent holds the jumbled letters inside it

parts.note: Asia is a continent

indicators.note: ruined means the letters of these words are wrecked and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Downing Street has wrecked the continent's homes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number Ten' looks like the Prime Minister's address; 'Number' is the definition, something that numbs, while 'ruined' scrambles TEN HAS into NAESTH.
explanation.definitionFit: A number here is something that numbs, and anaesthesia is the loss of feeling a numbing agent brings.

clue.text: Visit work briefly

indicators.note: briefly means the word for work is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: a calling is a vocation, one's work

explanation.surface: A short trip to the office.
explanation.definitionFit: To call in on someone is to pay a short visit.

clue.text: Revolt due to pact being broken

indicators.note: being broken means the letters of the treaty words are smashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: An uprising follows a broken treaty.
explanation.definitionFit: A coup d'etat is a sudden seizure of government power, a kind of revolt.

clue.text: Healthy, inspiring new boxer's one who may win

indicators.note: inspiring means breathing in, so the healthy word takes the other pieces inside

parts.note: fit means healthy
Muhammad Ali was the famous heavyweight boxer; boxer's gives his name with the S

explanation.surface: A fit young fighter could take the title.
explanation.definitionFit: A finalist has reached the last round of a contest, so is still in line for victory.

clue.text: Exploit voting procedure, producing one-sided document

parts.note: an exploit is a deed, a feat
a poll is a vote

explanation.surface: Taking advantage of how votes are cast to produce a biased paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exploit' reads as a verb but is the noun, a feat.
explanation.definitionFit: A deed poll is a legal deed made by one party only, often used to change one's name.

clue.text: Lacking bottle now, perhaps, ike some capsules

definitions.meaning: robbed of courage; bottle is British slang for nerve
the printed 'ike' is a typo for 'like'

explanation.surface: Losing one's nerve, rather like empty spacecraft.
explanation.definitionFit: Unmanned can mean deprived of courage, and also crewless, as in uncrewed space vehicles.

clue.text: Sentimental woman gets nothing in return

parts.note: Maud is a woman's name

indicators.note: in return means the word for nothing is read backwards

parts.note: nil means nothing

explanation.surface: A soppy woman receives nothing back.
explanation.definitionFit: Maudlin means tearfully or self-pityingly sentimental, often from drink.

clue.text: A few occupying Irish compound

indicators.note: occupying means the few word sits inside the Irish one

parts.note: a few means some

explanation.surface: A handful of people take over in Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: In chemistry an isomer is a compound with the same formula as another but a different structure.

clue.text: Huge insect covers a small distance

indicators.note: covers means the insect word goes round the other pieces

parts.note: a moth is an insect
MM, millimetre, is a small distance

explanation.surface: A giant bug travels only a short way.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective mammoth means enormous, from the vast extinct elephant.

clue.text: Mark runs animal food stores

indicators.note: stores means the food word keeps the runs letter inside it

parts.note: steak is food that comes from an animal
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Someone named Mark operates shops selling pet food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' poses as a man's name and 'runs' as a verb; 'animal food' is meat, not pet food.
explanation.definitionFit: A streak is a line or stripe of colour, a mark on a surface.

clue.text: Bent over London wife's nonsense

parts.note: to double over is to bend forward
'my old Dutch' is Cockney (East London) slang for one's wife

explanation.surface: A bent figure loudly mocks his London wife's chatter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'my old Dutch' is London Cockney slang for a wife.
explanation.definitionFit: Double Dutch is incomprehensible talk, gibberish that sounds like a foreign language.

clue.text: Ruin nearly all the planet

indicators.note: nearly all means the planet's name loses its final letter

parts.note: Mars is a planet

explanation.surface: Wrecking almost the entire world.
explanation.definitionFit: To mar something is to spoil or damage it.

clue.text: Row about bringing in first of frigates for overhaul

indicators.note: bringing in means the reversed row takes the letter inside
about means the row word is turned round

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats

indicators.note: first of means only the opening letter of frigates is used

explanation.surface: A quarrel about bringing warships in for repairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' suggests a quarrel; it is a line of seats, TIER, which 'about' turns to REIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A refit is a ship's overhaul, the repair and re-equipping of a vessel.

clue.text: Agree with head office quarry's been identified

parts.note: to tally is to agree or correspond

explanation.surface: Head office confirms that the stolen goods have been traced.
explanation.definitionFit: Tally-ho is the huntsman's cry when the fox, the hunted quarry, is sighted.

clue.text: That's the end of holiday working

indicators.note: the end of means the last letter of holiday is taken

parts.note: on means working, as a machine that is on

explanation.surface: The holiday is over; back to work.
explanation.definitionFit: Yon is an old or dialect word for that, pointing to something over there.

clue.text: Tablets not working by the sound of it — get less

indicators.note: by the sound of it means the words for tablets not working are spoken, giving a phrase that sounds the same

parts.note: E is slang for an ecstasy tablet, so Es are tablets, and off means not working

explanation.surface: The pills seem not to be working, so the effect is fading.
explanation.walkthrough: E's off, said out loud, matches the two-word answer.
explanation.definitionFit: When something eases off it diminishes or slackens, getting less intense.

clue.text: Retired musical group's section of joint

indicators.note: retired means going back, so the group's name is read backwards

parts.note: a nonet is a group of nine musicians

explanation.surface: A band that has stopped performing is part of a hip joint, in a sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenon is the projecting tongue that fits into a mortise to make a woodworking joint.

clue.text: Instantly fancy a go

parts.note: to fancy is to like
a go is a shot, an attempt

explanation.surface: An invitation to try something on the spot.
explanation.definitionFit: Like a shot is an idiom for very quickly, as fast as a bullet.
